en.title: Elizabeth Holmes Mania Fuels 'The Dropout' with 186% Viewership Surge
en.summary: A new documentary about Elizabeth Holmes has sent fans rushing back to Amanda Seyfried's Hulu series. 'The Dropout' saw a massive viewership spike, proving the enduring fascination with the Theranos saga.
en.body:
The enduring allure of the Elizabeth Holmes story continues to captivate audiences, with a recent surge in viewership for Hulu's limited series **The Dropout**. The Amanda Seyfried-led drama experienced an astonishing 186% increase in viewership in September compared to the previous month, according to Variety. This dramatic uptick is directly linked to the buzz surrounding A24's new documentary, **You Can See Everything**, which chronicles Holmes' final days before beginning her prison sentence.

Before the documentary's release, **The Dropout** was drawing a respectable 420,000 hours of watch time in August. However, the announcement and subsequent release of **You Can See Everything** on September 6th propelled the series to new heights, amassing 1.2 million hours watched in September alone. This demonstrates a powerful phenomenon: new content about a subject can significantly reignite interest in existing adaptations, even years after their initial release. The week of October 12th continued this trend, with an additional 422,000 hours watched, underscoring the sustained public fascination with the Theranos founder and the narrative surrounding her downfall.

## The Seyfried Paradox

While **The Dropout** soars, Amanda Seyfried herself has found herself at the center of a different kind of conversation. Her appearance in **You Can See Everything**, alongside Nathan Fielder, has drawn criticism from some viewers. These audiences have accused Seyfried of hypocrisy, pointing to her portrayal of Holmes in the Hulu series while seemingly defending the disgraced CEO as a victim of male manipulation in the documentary. This complex reaction highlights the nuanced ways audiences engage with true crime narratives and the public figures at their center, often blurring the lines between performance and personal opinion.

## What's Next

With the continued interest in Elizabeth Holmes, it's clear that the Theranos saga remains fertile ground for storytelling. While **The Dropout** has concluded its run, the success of **You Can See Everything** and the renewed attention on the series suggest that audiences are hungry for more. Whether this translates into new documentary projects or even further exploration of the legal and personal fallout remains to be seen, but the story is far from over for viewers.
